LOOK.text: Stairs to the upper floor. Every step has its own little light. Adrian never did anything halfway.

TALK.text: 'Anything up there I should know about?' The stairs creak. Noncommittal.

PICK.text: A tiny LED on the railing. Cute. Bolted on. Cute things usually are.

OPEN.text: A hidden compartment under one step. Empty. Somebody hid nothing, very carefully.

CLOSE.text: Stairs don't close. That's their whole appeal.

PUSH.text: I push the handrail. Sturdy. The one thing in this house that supports me.

PULL.text: I pull the railing. A bolt falls out. I put my hands in my pockets and walk away.

then.text: Fernando, freshly rained on. Glossy. Upright. Smug about it.

OPEN.text: I dig in the soil. Dirt. Roots. No clues. The plant looks violated.

CLOSE.text: I pat the soil back. Sorry, big guy.

PUSH.text: I push the pot. It scrapes the floor. Penny's head turns like an owl's.

PULL.text: I tug a leaf. The plant recoils. So does Penny.

GIVE.text: He takes water. Only water. I have none. We're both disappointed.

LOOK.text: Penny's desk. Five CRT monitors, a keyboard and a rubber stamp that just says 'NO'.

USE.text: I wiggle the mouse. Five screens wake up. One is Minesweeper. Penny is winning.

TALK.text: 'Show me the money!' Penny, without looking up: 'So would I. Payroll's been closed for three weeks.'

PICK.text: These CRTs weigh about 40 pounds each. My back says absolutely not.

OPEN.text: I open a drawer. Forms. Forms for requesting forms. Penny's filing system has a filing system.

CLOSE.text: I close the drawer before Penny opens an incident report.

PUSH.text: I push the desk. A CRT wobbles. Penny catches it one-handed without looking. Terrifying.

PULL.text: I pull out the keyboard tray. Crumbs, a stapler and a sticky note: 'FERNANDO: TUESDAYS'.

GIVE.text: Nothing to leave on Penny's desk. Except fingerprints. She'd dust for them.

LOOK.text: A vintage pendant lamp. It flickers every few seconds, like it's trying to tell me something. It isn't.

USE.text: I pull the chain. Dim. Bright. Dim. Penny is mentally filing a complaint.

TALK.text: The bulb buzzes. Possibly Morse code. Probably just dying.

PICK.text: Too high to reach without a ladder. Even on my tiptoes. Especially on my tiptoes.

OPEN.text: I can't open a ceiling light. That's not how lighting works.

CLOSE.text: Lights don't close. They turn off. Different verb, same disappointment.

PUSH.text: I push the air under the lamp. The air wins.

PULL.text: I jump and grab the chain. The lamp swings. Penny sighs the sigh of a pending form.

GIVE.text: I'd give the lamp a new bulb. I don't have one. I mostly have pockets.

LOOK.text: Checkered tiles. Brown, tan, brown, tan. Somebody here really likes order. I bet it's Penny.

USE.text: I tap-dance on the tiles. Great acoustics. Penny stares. Penny takes notes.

TALK.text: I kneel and whisper to the floor. 'Any secret basements down there?' The tiles remain tight-lipped.

PICK.text: I try to pry up a tile. Cemented. Penny watches me like I'm the reason they cemented it.

OPEN.text: One tile seems slightly loose but I can't lift it. Need better tools. Or worse morals.

CLOSE.text: The floor is already as closed as it gets.

PUSH.text: I stomp on the floor. Solid. No hollow sound. No secret passage. Just a sore heel.

PULL.text: I scratch at the grout between tiles. Nothing gives. Whoever laid these tiles was not messing around.

GIVE.text: The floor accepts only footsteps. And the occasional dropped coin that rolls under the desk forever.
